name: Metric to imperial conversion
seoTitle: Metric to imperial conversion Calculator: Free, With Steps
seoDesc: Metric to imperial conversion: work out temperature in Fahrenheit from the length in imperial units and the temperature in Celsius. A free conversion…
summary: The Metric to imperial conversion calculator turns the length in imperial units, the temperature in Celsius and more into temperature in Fahrenheit. It is built for a recipe, a shopping list, a travel plan or a form that asks for a unit you do not use. Every field is labelled the way you would say it out loud, so you can usually fill the form from memory and only look up the numbers you genuinely do not know.

sections.title: How does the Metric to imperial conversion calculator work?
sections.html:
The Metric to imperial conversion calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports temperature in Fahrenheit in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the type of conversion); then you type in the length in imperial units, the temperature in Celsius, the area in metric units and the volume in metric units.

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: What do you need to enter?
sections.html:
• Pick the option that matches your case — 5 options, such as length, area and volume. The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in feet. The unit chip switches it to any of the 34 supported units.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in Celsius. The unit chip switches it to any of the 28 supported units.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in square meters. The unit chip switches it to any of the 24 supported units.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in liters. The unit chip switches it to any of the 40 supported units.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in kilograms. The unit chip switches it to any of the 29 supported units.

1 field on this form is a choice rather than a number. Those choices decide which version of the calculation applies, so they are worth setting before you worry about the digits.

sections.title: The formula behind the Metric to imperial conversion calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Temperature in Fahrenheit=temperature in Celsius
Temperature in other scales=temperature in Celsius
Length in metric units=length in imperial units
Area in imperial units=area in metric units
Volume in imperial units=volume in metric units
Weight / Mass in imperial units=weight ÷ Mass in metric units

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.html:

  • Shown in kelvins, and convertible to any of the 28 units on that chip.
  • Shown in meters, and convertible to any of the 34 units on that chip.
  • Shown in square yards, and convertible to any of the 24 units on that chip.
  • Shown in gallons (US), and convertible to any of the 40 units on that chip.
  • Shown in pounds, and convertible to any of the 29 units on that chip.

Before doubting the arithmetic, check the inputs: a unit chip on the wrong setting, a drop-down left at its default, or a percentage typed as a whole number rather than a decimal will each shift the answer by a clean power of ten.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • Length, opening in meters
  • Length, opening in feet
  • Temperature, opening in Celsius
  • Temperature, opening in Fahrenheit
  • Temperature, opening in kelvins
  • Area, opening in square meters
  • Area, opening in square yards
  • Volume, opening in liters

Display rounding is separate from calculation rounding: the digits you see are shortened, the value behind them is not. Numbers far from everyday size are shown in scientific notation so the significant digits stay readable.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Metric to imperial conversion calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Converting a figure someone quoted you so you can compare it
  • Filling in a form that asks for imperial or metric values
  • Reading a recipe written in units you do not use
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the length in imperial units, the temperature in Celsius and the area in metric units — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Metric to imperial conversion calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns temperature in Fahrenheit, derived from the length in imperial units, the temperature in Celsius and the area in metric units. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Metric to imperial conversion calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the length in imperial units, the temperature in Celsius, the area in metric units and the volume in metric units, which is 6 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter length in metric units in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Length in metric units opens in meters and the chip beside it offers 34 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There is one choice to make (1 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

faq.q: Is the Metric to imperial conversion calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
